html:
October 8, 2026

Pentagon directs CENTCOM to prepare for renewed major strikes on Iran

tags: war, politics, defence
sources: @hunteralexanderhowell, @oafnation_actual

The Pentagon has told U.S. Central Command to complete preparations for possible renewed major combat operations against Iran, with potential targets including nuclear facilities and energy infrastructure. Reporting indicates the planning is being coordinated with the Israeli military, and that Trump spoke with Prime Minister Netanyahu about the plans. No new strikes have been authorized and no date has been set; the directive signals further preparation rather than a decision to attack.

ICE investigated voter registration groups as armed guards deploy to post offices

tags: politics, surveillance, legal
sources: @aaronparnas

Documents obtained by Democracy Forward show ICE's Homeland Security Investigations has been probing hundreds of non-profit voter registration groups, prioritizing battleground states such as Pennsylvania and searching databases for derogatory information on them, with undercover agents considered. ICE obtained more than 48 million records through Heather Honey, a prominent 2020 election denier, and some of the data may have been fed into Palantir systems. Separately, nearly a thousand armed private security guards have been deployed to post offices ahead of election day, working for a contractor with a history of alleged human rights abuses. The head of the Postal Police Officers Association warned the guards are operating without Postal Service supervision.

Tina Peters met Trump to discuss nationwide ballot seizure plan

tags: politics, legal
sources: @aaronparnas

Tina Peters, the former Colorado county clerk convicted over an effort to overturn election results and later pardoned by Governor Jared Polis, met with Trump in the Oval Office on Monday to discuss a plan to seize ballots nationwide and conduct a hand recount, according to Colorado journalist Kyle Clark. Her attorney, Peter Ticktin, said the discussions included strategy for a potential civil war and said he has pushed the president to declare a national emergency and consider martial law. Neither a nationwide ballot seizure nor the measures described are within presidential legal authority.

Democrats hold strongest midterm polling position in nearly two decades

tags: politics, economy
sources: @groundnews

With a month until the midterms, Trump's approval is at an all-time low across both of his terms and gas prices are approaching record levels, producing the most unfavorable polling environment for Republicans in nearly 20 years. Senate races are unexpectedly close in Nebraska, Kansas, Iowa and Alaska, while Republicans have largely pulled spending from Georgia and North Carolina, and Democrats are slight favorites in Ohio and Texas. Cost of living is the dominant issue for voters, and special elections show a Democratic enthusiasm advantage that could be magnified by lower midterm turnout. A systematic polling error remains possible, though surveys were largely accurate in the last two midterms when Trump was not on the ballot.

Trump says he could do very bad things to Obama, Biden and Clinton

tags: politics, legal
sources: @aaronparnas, @ericmoutsos

Trump said he could have done "very bad things" to Hillary Clinton, Joe Biden and Barack Obama but chose not to out of respect for the office, adding that after being impeached twice, "I can do whatever I want if I want." He described the conduct of those figures as "very illegal" without specifying what action he was contemplating. The president does not hold the authority to take the kinds of actions the remarks imply.

Companies backed by Trump's sons tied to more than $6 billion in federal contracts

tags: politics, defence, markets
sources: @oafnation_actual

An ABC News analysis found that companies backed by investment firms connected to Donald Trump Jr. and Eric Trump hold more than $6 billion in active or promised government contracts. Firms including Unusual Machines, Powerus and Anduril, which list the brothers as notable investors, have won defense work spanning drones, rare-earth mining, quantum computing and robotics, and several had never previously held federal contracts. The brothers deny influencing federal procurement, and some of the companies were government contractors before their investments.

Federal judge blocks $84 billion in expanded immigration fines

tags: immigration, legal
sources: @oafnation_actual

A federal judge has blocked the Trump administration's expanded immigration penalty system, which issued more than 103,000 fines totaling roughly $84 billion. Individual penalties under the program reached as high as $1.8 million.

Guilfoyle asked Trump donor to pay $100,000 credit card bill before confirmation

tags: politics, legal
sources: @aaronparnas

Wall Street Journal reporting says Kimberly Guilfoyle, now U.S. Ambassador to Greece, pressured Trump donor Eric Dieters to pay a $100,000 American Express bill ahead of her Senate confirmation hearing, suggesting a wire transfer to avoid leaving a paper trail. Guilfoyle allegedly offered to use her connections to assist the donor with IRS and Justice Department matters. Dieters was repeatedly warned against documenting the arrangement on the grounds it could cost her the ambassadorship.

Utah coal county residents fight nuclear-powered data center project

tags: climate, tech, health
sources: @carolinegleich

Valar Atomics, an experimental nuclear startup, has secured a 100-year lease on a square mile of state land near Wellington in Carbon County, Utah, as part of a plan covering roughly 9,000 acres of public and state land for nuclear reactors, fuel processing and data centers. Residents say they learned of the plan on September 30 and have had little opportunity for public comment, raising concerns about proximity to homes and recreation areas, long-term nuclear waste storage, protected species habitat and health effects. The company's test reactor was cleared without an environmental impact study, and Valar has sued the Nuclear Regulatory Commission seeking to remove its small reactors from federal safety licensing. A local physician and pathologist with 35 years in the area said questions about industrial disease need answers before the community accepts the project.

DNC sues over taxpayer-funded ads promoting Trump

tags: politics, legal, media
sources: @groundnews

The Democratic National Committee sued the Trump administration on Wednesday, alleging that taxpayer-funded television ads promoting the president constitute illegal government propaganda. The suit seeks to halt federal spending on the campaign and have the ads declared unlawful. The spots have cost more than $12 million since September according to AdImpact, with $20 million in Homeland Security funding allocated; Trump defended them as positive promotion and said MAGA Inc. would fund them going forward, telling reporters "we'll decide" when asked about reimbursing past spending.

White House proposes mandatory minimum sentences for federal benefit fraud

tags: politics, legal, health
sources: @groundnews

The White House sent Congress legislation requiring minimum prison terms for fraud involving Medicare, Medicaid and Social Security. Terms would scale with losses: one year below $40,000, two years from $40,000 to $250,000, and 20 years at $100 million or more, with every violation carrying a possible life sentence. The measure would also make state officers or employees who knowingly or recklessly ignore fraud personally liable, including for financial damages. Congress must approve the proposal for it to become law.

Pentagon denies senator access to largest US base in the Middle East

tags: defence, politics
sources: @oafnation_actual

The Pentagon denied Senator Chris Murphy access to Al Udeid Air Base in Qatar, the largest American military installation in the region. Murphy says he was also denied a briefing on the Iran war. The Pentagon says the restriction stems from a region-wide travel directive issued in March and was not specific to Murphy.

US troops ran low on ammunition defending Kuwait base from Iranian attacks

tags: war, defence
sources: @oafnation_actual

New reporting says U.S. soldiers at Camp Buehring in Kuwait ran critically low on .50-caliber ammunition while defending the base against Iranian attacks. More than 100 troops remained at the base before withdrawing into the Kuwaiti desert.

RFK Jr.'s NIH sent nearly $800,000 to project tied to Russian plague lab

tags: health, politics
sources: @aaronparnas

An investigation by the watchdog group White Coat Waste reports that the National Institutes of Health awarded $779,689 to the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign in 2025 and 2026 for research conducted in partnership with Russia's state-run Institute of Cytology and Genetics. Federal records show about $389,000 disbursed in July of last year and a further $389,000 last month. The Russian institute previously worked on plague research alongside the Irkutsk Anti-Plague Research Institute, where a scientist recently died. Republicans criticized Dr. Anthony Fauci for comparable foreign research funding arrangements during the COVID-19 pandemic.

Project 2025 author Russ Vought drives executive branch consolidation from OMB

tags: politics, climate, government
sources: @total.hypocrisy

Office of Management and Budget Director Russ Vought, an author of Project 2025 and close collaborator with the Heritage Foundation, wrote the chapter arguing the president must reclaim control of the executive branch from career federal employees and redistribute power to states, cities and churches. Actions attributed to his influence include the first-day executive order shutting the White House Gender Policy Council, the elimination of the State Department office overseeing climate talks, the abandonment of the social cost of carbon metric, rewriting environmental review rules to speed approvals for pipelines and highways, and a dramatic staff reduction at the National Security Council targeting those seen as insufficiently loyal. Trump has praised Vought publicly and said "big surprises" are coming.

Appeals court shields government from suit over FBI raid on wrong home

tags: legal, policing
sources: @oafnation_actual

An FBI SWAT team raided the wrong house, held an innocent family at gunpoint and terrified a seven-year-old boy, with the team leader attributing the error to his GPS. Nine years later, a federal appeals court ruled the government is shielded from the family's lawsuit, though the individual agent may still face liability.

Transportation Department ties transit grants to marriage and birth rates

tags: politics, economy
sources: @groundnews

The U.S. Transportation Department proposed increasing federal transit grants by 10% for communities with above-average marriage and birth rates while imposing stricter project deadlines, affecting 40 existing projects in a program funding rail and bus systems. Democratic Senator Patty Murray warned the policy could cut funding for projects in Washington, Boston, Silicon Valley and Austin, citing research suggesting the criteria would favor wealthier, predominantly white communities over underserved urban neighborhoods. The department, which distributes roughly $20 billion in annual transit grants, said the changes would accelerate construction and direct money toward growing communities.

Alito calls same-sex marriage ruling the turning point against religious liberty

tags: legal, politics
sources: @aaronparnas

Supreme Court Justice Samuel Alito writes in his new book that Obergefell v. Hodges, the decision establishing same-sex marriage rights, was "perhaps the decisive point in our nation's turn against religious liberty." The comments come as Justice Clarence Thomas has signaled openness to overturning the ruling and conservative groups press the court to revisit it, though there do not appear to be five votes to do so. Legal experts note the court's religious liberty docket over the past decade has consistently ruled in favor of religious claimants.

Cornell Jane Doe receives death threats as rally demands action

tags: legal, policing
sources: @groundnews, @aaronparnas

Hundreds of Cornell University students, faculty and community members rallied Monday in support of a student who alleges she was gang-raped by fraternity members in 2024, demanding stronger action on campus sexual violence, an independent review of the university's response and the president's resignation. The student, identified as Jane Doe, sued Cornell, seven Chi Phi members and others last month, alleging the university failed to investigate and punish those involved; the accused men denied wrongdoing, with some saying the activity was consensual. Governor Kathy Hochul appointed Attorney General Letitia James as special prosecutor after authorities reopened the criminal investigation. She has since received texts and calls, reported by the New York Post, threatening to shoot members of her family unless she drops the lawsuit, some containing specific names and addresses.

FBI says it disrupted ISIS-inspired plot at Mall of America

tags: policing, legal
sources: @oafnation_actual

The FBI says it stopped an ISIS-inspired plot to kill up to 60 people at the Mall of America. An 18-year-old suspect was arrested after buying a disabled AK-47 and ammunition from an undercover agent for $600. Messages cited in the case include a pledge of allegiance to an ISIS leader.

Former CIA official pleads guilty in $194 million fraud scheme

tags: legal, government
sources: @oafnation_actual

A former senior CIA official, David Rush, has pleaded guilty in a $194 million government fraud scheme. When the FBI searched his home, agents recovered 298 gold bars and more than $2.1 million in cash.

Mike Johnson signals he may leave Congress if Republicans lose the House

tags: politics
sources: @aaronparnas

House Speaker Mike Johnson told a Fox News reporter that if Republicans lose their majority, "I don't know what my next chapter of life is," saying he might return to Shreveport to start a law and business practice. Republicans are currently on track to lose the House, which would cost Johnson the speakership though not his seat.

Trump proposes converting private Florida golf club into presidential retreat

tags: politics, government
sources: @oafnation_actual

Trump wants part of his private Florida golf club converted into a presidential retreat for future presidents and visiting foreign leaders. His company would fund construction and provide government access free of charge while the private golf operation continues next door. Trump said military and Secret Service officials suggested the idea for security reasons; local approval is still required.

Republican Senate candidates ask donors to cover fuel costs

tags: politics, economy
sources: @aaronparnas

Fundraising emails obtained by Midas Touch show Republican Senate candidates asking supporters to pay for campaign fuel. Alaska Senator Dan Sullivan's appeal says donations will "pay for gas as we visit isolated rural areas," Susan Collins' team asks for $5 to "help us put gas in the tank," and Georgia candidate Mike Collins asks supporters to "put some diesel in the tank." Gasoline and diesel prices have continued to rise amid the war in Iran and administration energy policies the candidates have supported.

Nevada candidate who misstated Bronze Star was relieved of Air Force command

tags: politics, defence
sources: @oafnation_actual

Nevada congressional candidate David Flippo recently acknowledged that his campaign materials falsely described his Bronze Star as awarded "for valor." His former group commander now says he relieved Flippo from squadron command in 2008 for "loss of confidence in his ability to command." The Reno Gazette Journal says it confirmed the account with Flippo's replacement.

Vance struggles to define socialism when asked

tags: politics
sources: @aaronparnas

Asked to define socialism, Vice President J.D. Vance said the term is hard to define and that classically it concerns prioritizing workers. He then said that in the American context it means wanting "to replace American workers with foreign workers" and wanting "boys to play in girls' sports." The remarks drew criticism for not describing the economic doctrine.
